summary: Validated (first patch attempt hit the same malformed-hunk error and was re-issued cleanly; validate --run <run> --submission update40.json → valid=true). Final record of this run, and it narrows the one question I had left paused. That question asks whether a peer that cannot handle the pre-vote RPC returns an error containing the substring the candidate treats as a granted pre-vote; deciding it needs the counterpart version's error text, which is outside the snapshot. This record shows why the retained mixed-version pre-vote test cannot stand in for it: the variation it exercises is a configuration flag applied to nodes built from the current source (raft-compat/prevote_test.go:36-58 and the upgrade loop at 60-130), so those peers are protocol-capable and implement the handler, answering pre-vote requests normally rather than producing an unsupported-command error; the peers that could produce it are the older-version ones whose replaced module directory is missing from the captured tree (recorded earlier), and the compatibility module is not even buildable from the snapshot. What the test does assert is cluster-level behaviour in a mixed configuration — leader unchanged while followers are replaced one by one with logs still applied, and a new leader elected after the old leader is removed, with a comment attributing that election's speed to the absence of pre-vote — which is consistent with the feature working in mixed clusters but does not exercise the fallback's trigger. Recorded as one Fact plus an unresolved interpretation that keeps the pause and sharpens the resume condition (the counterpart transport's unknown-rpc-type error text, or a retained observation of one pre-vote exchange with such a peer), with counterevidence preserved and no defect claimed. That closes the run: source-grounded findings and bounded conclusions across consensus formation/progress and authority transitions, protective-mechanism and coverage negatives, durable corrections where later evidence narrowed earlier assertions, and the contrary evidence that one of my own records concerned an issue the repository already acknowledges.
